question: According to the GSEs' August 2024 PMIERs update (Guidance 2024-01), what is the implementation phase-in schedule, and what substantive change does it make to the PMIERs standards?
expected: The August 21, 2024 PMIERs update refined the Available Assets definition by introducing new investment-risk deductions based on asset class and credit rating (more granular bond credit-quality and liquidity tiers) and establishing new limits on assets backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate. The phase-in is over 24 months: 25% effective March 31, 2025; 50% effective September 30, 2025; 75% effective March 31, 2026; and 100% effective September 30, 2026. Separately, the COVID-19 Disaster Related Capital Charge for COVID-19 Defaulted Loans was eliminated effective March 31, 2025.
answer:
Guidance 2024-01 (issued August 21, 2024, effective March 31, 2025) makes two changes:

**Substantive change.** It tightens Section 703's definition of Available Assets by: requiring all bonds to be rated (by S&P, Moody's, Fitch, A.M. Best, DBRS, or KBRA) — unrated bonds are ineligible; introducing a graded haircut table by rating (0.20% for AAA up to 100% for CCC+ and below); excluding mortgage insurance-linked notes, all non-agency RMBS, and bonds below specified rating/term thresholds; raising the discount on common/preferred shares from 25% to 50%; and adding new concentration limits (GSE debt/MBS ≤ 25% of Available Assets, ABS ≤ 20%, sub-investment-grade bonds + common/preferred shares aggregate ≤ 5%, non-agency CMBS ≤ 5%, eligible surplus notes capped at 9% of Minimum Required Assets, COLI ≤ 10% of risk-based required asset amount).

**Phase-in schedule.** The new rules phase in over six quarters:

| Quarter ending | Add-back of prior framework | Implied phase-in of new rules |
|---|---|---|
| March 31, 2025 & June 30, 2025 | 75% | 25% |
| September 30, 2025 & December 31, 2025 | 50% | 50% |
| March 31, 2026 & June 30, 2026 | 25% | 75% |
| September 30, 2026 onward | 0% | 100% |

*(Source: INDUSTRY_PMIERS_GUIDANCE_2024-01)*
